annotations.count_cue: 39 included pseudepigrapha = the 39 entries in the TOC (35 under Part I + 4 under Part II), each a fresh English translation of an ancient noncanonical text. PROGRAMMATICALLY corroborated: the per-text opener 'A new translation and introduction' resolves 38× case-insensitively + the 1 variant 'Introduction and a new translation of the Armenian version' (Queen of Sheba) = 39, exactly matching the TOC. Each text contributes exactly one translation body (a few texts present multiple recensions inside it — Adam Octipartite has Latin/Slavonic/Irish under explicit 'Translation: …' subheads, the only 3 'Translation:'-colon headers in the volume — but the translated WORK is one unit). The translation body is the ancient text itself, distinct from the editor's introduction that precedes it and the apparatus that follows.

annotations.count_cue: Two distinct per-text apparatus systems, both present for most of the 39 texts: (1) NUMBERED introduction footnotes (1., 2., 3., … keyed to the scholarly essay) and (2) LETTERED translation notes (a., b., c., … critical/text-variant apparatus keyed to the translated ancient text, e.g. '"to me"; Greek omits'). expected_count is null: a single cardinality is not cleanly extractable because the two systems interleave, restart per text, and the lettered notes reuse single-letter labels that recur thousands of times (no per-instance content anchor is unique). Presence + the two-system distinction is the contract.
